findings.body: The provider translation still infers the refusal reason from which operand failed rather than why it failed. For example, `Actual > governed-financial.percentage` is rejected by the provider as `selectionMeasureFilterOperandNotAllowed` (`bedrock.provider.ts:362-369`), but this branch maps every such result to `UnknownMeasure`; Percentage exists and should produce `NotComparable` and the `%`-specific sentence. Conversely, an unknown left-hand measure is mapped to `NotComparable`. Thus provider-door refusals and structured logs disagree with the canonical helper/direct door. The new test only covers a non-comparable left operand and unknown right operand, missing these reversed cases.
findings.title: Not done: A comparison that cannot be honoured is refused with a stated reason, never silently dropped

findings.body: The empty-answer test still injects an empty table through `FakeExecutor`, so it does not prove that real filtered SQL execution reaches the API as a successful zero-row answer with the stated message. The story assigns that warehouse/API/browser proof (functional matrix row 6) to MEASURE-FILTER-SURFACES, making this a later-task test gap rather than a blocker for this branch.
findings.title: Later: prove the empty Ask answer through MEASURE-FILTER-SURFACES
